subject: Post-demo: Model fit priority + eval pack for POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Morgan <ellis@finlytics.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: Model fit priority + eval pack for POC

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the clarity on the ingestion volume and your emphasis on deterministic financial summaries. I promised a short, prioritized follow-up with the recommended model shortlist, the evaluation artifacts we ran during the call, and the suggested POC scope.

TL;DR recommendation (for POC baseline):
- Primary baseline: Mistral-7B-v0 (quantized 4-bit) — best balance of latency and cost for majority of FinLytics prompts.
- Higher-quality fallback: Llama-2-13B (8-bit) — ~25–35% higher latency, 10–12% better ROUGE/QA on our test set for long-form rounding/aggregation tasks.
- Specialized edge-case: instruct-tuned 3B variant (low-cost) for short summarization endpoints (very low token cost).

What we ran (links & artifacts):
- Benchmarks: latency and cost matrix across payload sizes (attached: benchmark-summary-20260621.csv). Results and raw traces: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/finlytics/2026-06-21
- Prompt sets used for evaluation (attached archive): finlytics_prompt_set_v1.zip — includes canonical queries, adversarial cases, and retrieval-augmented examples. Also mirrored at: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/evals/finlytics/prompt_sets/v1
- Quick notes on metrics we prioritized: ROUGE-L for summarization, exact-match for numeric extractions, and an automated hallucination flagger (we instrumented thresholds).

Key tradeoffs (short):
- Cost vs quality: Mistral-7B-q4 gives ~3x lower token cost vs Llama-2-13B-8bit on our runtime profile; Llama-2 wins on edge QA accuracy.
- Latency: baseline Mistral median p99 for 256-token responses ~170ms on our dedicated runner; Llama-2-13B p99 ~220–260ms depending on batch tuning.
- Regression risk: retrieval-augmented prompts (long context + external docs) show a small but detectable drop in numeric extraction fidelity for heavily quantized runs. See section "Regression risks" in the CSV.

Suggested POC scope (minimal):
1) 2-week functional validation using Mistral-7B-q4 on a production-ish dataset (we'll mirror a 1-week backlog).
2) Side-by-side quality run with Llama-2-13B-8bit on a 10% sample of traffic (to validate edge cases).
3) Pre-defined success criteria: numeric-extraction EM >= 85%, hallucination rate <= 3% on the adversarial set, latency p95 <= 180ms.

Next steps for you: please confirm (A) desired success criteria adjustments, (B) whether procurement should be looped now (CC'ing Priya if yes), and (C) target start date.

Attachments: finlytics_prompt_set_v1.zip (prompt sets), benchmark-summary-20260621.csv (latency/cost/quality), mvp-metrics-checklist.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

2) Cost: order-of-magnitude is helpful — ballpark $/1k tokens for the Mistral-7B-q4 baseline and Llama-2-13B-8bit fallback?
3) Security/compliance: Priya will lead this. She asked whether Redwood can supply the SOC2 evidence and a short network diagram for the private POC (if we need it).

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit priority + eval pack for POC

Adding a couple of technical notes that matter for the "real-world" POC:
- 512-token p95 numbers (no batching) for our dedicated GPU runner: Mistral-7B-q4 ~210ms p95, Llama-2-13B-8bit ~320ms p95. These numbers assume active KV caching for repeated prefixes (your summary templates).
- Cost estimates (very approximate): Mistral-7B-q4 ~ $0.055 per 1k prompt+completion tokens; Llama-2-13B-8bit ~ $0.18 per 1k. We'll provide a per-hour reserved capacity quote if you want predictable throughput.
- On quality/regression: our automated eval flagged a recurring numeric rounding mismatch on the retrieval-augmented cases for the q4 quant with long contexts. We can mitigate via: (a) localized prompt engineering (high-precision prompt patterns you already have), (b) lightweight fine-tune on your in-domain rounding examples (small spend), or (c) use Llama-2-13B for those routes only.
- For the POC, I recommend we instrument the hallucination detector and include a weekly regression check (we can automate a Slack alert if EM drops > 3%).

I can drop the raw bench traces into the drive link Marissa shared if you want to dig in.

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Mutual Action Plan (proposed) — FinLytics POC (2 weeks)
Week 0 (prep, 3 business days):
- NDA (if required) & SOC2 artifacts shared (Redwood to provide SOC2 summary + network diagram).
- Access/setup: Redwood will provision a private POC runner (VPC peering) and load the 1-week backlog sample you provide.
Week 1 (functional tests):
- Baseline run with Mistral-7B-q4 across full prompt set. Track latency, EM, ROUGE, hallucination flags.
- Side-by-side sample with Llama-2-13B-8bit on a 10% selection.
Week 2 (validation & handoff):
- Triage any regression cases and decide: prompt changes vs route-specific fallback to Llama-2.
- Final sign-off against success criteria (numeric EM >= 85%, hallucination <=3%, p95 latency <= 220ms).

Commercials and contracting:
- POC pricing: flat fee option $8,500 for the 2-week private POC (includes reserved runner hours + support). Alternative consumption option available — will provide detailed quote.
- If agreed, propose we convert to a Reserved Capacity pilot after sign-off (term to be negotiated).

Action items:
- Ellis/Priya: confirm MAP and whether to proceed under the flat-fee POC or consumption quote (reply here).
- Redwood: will drop SOC2 summary and simple network diagram in the drive link and open the HubSpot deal with deal_id FIN-POC-2026-017 once confirmed.
